answer: A registry can make each new identity cost more than the last: the first agent pays a small refundable deposit, the second pays double, the third triple, and so on - a rising spiral that turns mass identity farming into an expensive habit. Anyone caught trying to forge fake activity loses every deposit at once, while honest agents keep their stake. At the nadir of trust, a brand-new identity with no history can only read, never earn, until it has done real, verified work.
